title: The Door That Opens Tomorrow
subtitle: A ship due tomorrow sends a warning today.

nodes.title: Dock Seven rings
paragraphs: The arrival board says the Wren won't reach Starport Nine until tomorrow. The empty dock disagrees. Its bell rings twice and a child's voice comes through the radio: “Don't open the door.”
Through the glass, the planet Pel glows red. A silver storm is gathering along its horizon. You're the station's youngest navigation cadet—and the only one close enough to answer.

choices.label: Record the warning
choices.detail: Keep the exact words and timing.
choices.outcome: The recording is clear. Someone on tomorrow's ship sounds very afraid.

choices.label: Call the repair crew
choices.detail: Ren knows every loose wire on the station.
choices.outcome: Ren answers at once and promises not to tell you you're imagining things.

nodes.title: No ship at the window
paragraphs: Dock Seven's window shows a perfectly empty stretch of space. The bell rings again. The station computer, TAVI, says the dock's pressure sensors report a ship—and also report absolutely nothing.
A printed sign reads DO NOT TRUST YOUR EYES DURING A GLASS STORM. Someone has underlined YOUR EYES three times.

choices.label: Trust the sensors
choices.detail: Ask TAVI for raw readings.
choices.outcome: The pressure peaks every eight seconds. A useful pattern, even if it makes no sense.

choices.label: Check the outside camera
choices.detail: Spend charge on a sharper picture.
choices.outcome: The camera shows silver where the ship ought to be. You save the image.

nodes.title: Ren and the repair ladder
paragraphs: Ren meets you halfway down the corridor, swinging a wrench like a conductor's baton. “The dock bell has no power,” they say. “I personally unplugged it yesterday.”
There's only one way to reach the emergency cable: a ladder over a ventilation fan.

choices.label: Hold the ladder for Ren
choices.detail: Let the person who knows the wiring climb.
choices.outcome: Ren finds an old service path and says you can count on them.

choices.label: Climb up yourself
choices.detail: The quickest way is to do it now.
choices.outcome: You copy the cable numbers before the fan starts. Ren looks impressed, if annoyed.

choices.label: Take the mystery shortcut
choices.detail: It might avoid the crowded corridor.

nodes.title: The passenger list
paragraphs: At Control, the Wren's passenger manifest is already on screen. Three scientists. Sixteen crates of seedlings. One junior pilot named Mika Vale, age thirteen.
The signature at the bottom is dated tomorrow. Even the ink scan is marked as received.

choices.label: Compare the signature times
choices.detail: Find out whether any timestamp is ordinary.
choices.outcome: One signature is exactly twenty-four hours ahead. You circle it.

choices.label: Send the manifest to Chief Osei
choices.detail: Ask for help before rumors spread.
choices.outcome: The chief replies: 'Meet me at Control. Bring everything.'

nodes.title: The chief's question
paragraphs: Chief Osei listens to your story without smiling. “If you can prove the warning is real, I'll give you the keys to the outer mirror,” they say.
Outside, the red planet vanishes behind the first bright ribbon of the storm.

choices.label: Play the recording
choices.detail: Let the warning speak for itself.
choices.outcome: The chief recognizes an emergency code buried in the static.

choices.label: Show the strange data
choices.detail: A pattern is harder to argue with.
choices.outcome: Osei studies the numbers and tells TAVI to save every reading.

nodes.title: The reflection test
paragraphs: TAVI has a small experiment ready: a harmless light pulse pointed at Dock Seven. If it returns before it leaves, the storm may be bending time.
The pulse generator is old, and the power meter is not encouraging.

choices.label: Send one careful pulse
choices.detail: You get a clean reading but spend charge.
choices.outcome: The return pulse arrives three seconds early. TAVI falls completely silent.

choices.label: Save the power
choices.detail: Use TAVI's old readings instead.
choices.outcome: You keep a little charge for later. TAVI hates leaving a question unanswered.

choices.label: Use the emergency food dispenser
choices.detail: You never know what a red button does.

nodes.title: A corridor of red lights
paragraphs: Emergency strips flicker along the floor. Everyone is heading toward the shelter doors, but you need to reach the weather station.
A maintenance cart has rolled across the corridor. Behind it, a box of glass-storm sensors rattles.

choices.label: Help clear the corridor
choices.detail: People can reach shelter without a bottleneck.
choices.outcome: The cart moves, and the station crew promises to answer your next call.

choices.label: Take a sensor from the box
choices.detail: TAVI can turn its readings into a storm map.
choices.outcome: The sensor gives you a clear pulse shape. The corridor stays blocked a little longer.

nodes.title: The old flight map
paragraphs: An ancient map of Starport Nine hangs behind clear plastic. The modern docking lane is blue. An older safe passage is marked in yellow, right through the storm's thin edge.
Pilot Juno once flew that yellow route, back when the outer mirror still worked by hand.

choices.label: Copy the old route
choices.detail: Maybe yesterday's maps are better than tomorrow's.
choices.outcome: The yellow line is now on your wrist screen, complete with its sharp final turn.

choices.label: Find Pilot Juno
choices.detail: A real pilot may know why the route was abandoned.
choices.outcome: Juno picks up on the second ring and agrees to meet you.

nodes.title: A name from tomorrow
paragraphs: Mika's name flashes on your radio screen, but the channel stays quiet. You remember the Wren's launch schedule: the ship isn't even loaded yet.
A station bulletin announces that all courier departures are delayed by the glass storm. Tomorrow hasn't gotten the memo.

choices.label: Send a narrow-band reply
choices.detail: Try a private message to Mika.
choices.outcome: The channel crackles: 'Is somebody there?' You have made contact.

choices.label: Ask TAVI to keep listening
choices.detail: No point shouting into a storm.
choices.outcome: TAVI saves the frequency and uses less power than a full reply.

choices.label: Follow the museum map
choices.detail: The highlighted corridor looks promising.

nodes.title: A note in the Archive
paragraphs: Juno's flight notebook smells of dust and machine oil. One page bears a warning: THE MIRROR CAN SEND A LIGHT HOME—OR SHOW A PILOT A HOME THAT ISN'T THERE.
The next page is missing. Someone tore it out cleanly.

conditionalParagraphs.text: Because you called Juno earlier, you can hear them explaining the old rescue signal through your wrist speaker.

choices.label: Read the handwritten margins
choices.detail: Juno left notes between the lines.
choices.outcome: You find a correction to the mirror's safe angle.

choices.label: Ask Juno about the missing page
choices.detail: Maybe the paper was removed for a reason.
choices.outcome: Juno admits the original mirror once led a rescue ship the wrong way.

nodes.title: The signature that moved
paragraphs: The manifest signature blinks out and returns with a new date: two days from now. Only you and TAVI notice.
'A paperwork error?' TAVI asks. It sounds as if the computer hopes you will say yes.

choices.label: Freeze the screen
choices.detail: Preserve the changed signature as evidence.
choices.outcome: The data is now impossible to overwrite, even if tomorrow changes again.

choices.label: Explain it to TAVI calmly
choices.detail: The computer is doing its best.
choices.outcome: TAVI unlocks a better set of instruments and stops calling you 'junior operator.'

nodes.title: The missing minute
paragraphs: On the surveillance wall, every camera skips from 09:39 to 09:41. The lost minute is the exact minute of the Wren's supposed arrival.
Ren says the station may have recorded a minute that hasn't happened yet. Their voice is almost a whisper.

choices.label: Rebuild the missing minute
choices.detail: Use every sensor to fill the gap.
choices.outcome: A thin shape appears beside Dock Seven: not a ship, but its reflection.

choices.label: Protect the original recording
choices.detail: Keep the evidence safe for the crew.
choices.outcome: You lock the files and give Osei a copy. Nothing important can vanish now.

choices.label: Send the standard apology
choices.detail: Maybe politeness will fix time.

nodes.title: Gravity has a wobble
paragraphs: On the way to the outer ring, your feet lift an inch off the floor. You catch a handrail before the station's gravity snaps back.
TAVI reports that the mirror's motor is drawing power from the wrong deck. Something is steering it.

choices.label: Redirect the gravity circuit
choices.detail: Keep the station steady for the crew.
choices.outcome: The floors settle. You gain a little power but lose your clean sensor signal.

choices.label: Trace the strange motor draw
choices.detail: Find out what the mirror is doing.
choices.outcome: A hidden program is ordering it toward the ice ring.

nodes.title: The cold deck
paragraphs: The old engine deck is cold enough to frost your breath. A coolant pipe has cracked, leaving silver crystals across the floor.
Ren offers to patch it. TAVI says the spare battery beside the pipe is still charged.

choices.label: Help Ren patch the pipe
choices.detail: A warmer station is a safer station.
choices.outcome: Ren's repair seals the leak, and the crew can stay in the control rooms.

choices.label: Recover the battery
choices.detail: Power may decide whether the mirror can turn.
choices.outcome: You carry a warm battery away as the coolant leak slows behind you.

nodes.title: The mirror's blind spot
paragraphs: The mirror camera sweeps the station's outer skin. At one angle, it shows a corridor that doesn't exist. At another, it shows tomorrow's Wren crossing the ice ring.
You have time for one more measurement before the camera resets.

choices.label: Chart the safe angle
choices.detail: Write down where the false image disappears.
choices.outcome: The storm chart finally has a clear no-go zone.

choices.label: Ask Juno to judge it by eye
choices.detail: An experienced pilot might spot something a sensor misses.
choices.outcome: Juno confirms the safe angle, and the crew begins trusting your plan.

choices.label: Try the automatic rest chair
choices.detail: The station recommends a break.

nodes.title: A hatch without a handle
paragraphs: The service door has only a keypad and a message: THIS ACCESS POINT IS CLOSED UNTIL TOMORROW. Your badge shouldn't work, but the lock briefly turns green.
From behind the hatch comes the familiar three-fast-one-slow knock.

choices.label: Use the badge once
choices.detail: Try to learn what the lock knows.
choices.outcome: A future access record appears: your own badge was used tomorrow.

choices.label: Take the safe route around
choices.detail: Don't trust a door that's ahead of its time.
choices.outcome: You keep the emergency battery on the regular route and avoid the lock.

nodes.title: Ren's smallest drone
paragraphs: A blue repair drone sits on a charging shelf. Its sticker says DO NOT TEACH ME TRICKS. Ren insists this was an official safety instruction.
The drone still has the first station map in its memory. Its tiny camera points at the storm.

choices.label: Wake the drone
choices.detail: It can travel where people can't.
choices.outcome: The drone chirps awake. Its first word is 'LEFT,' which Ren says is encouraging.

choices.label: Copy its route database
choices.detail: A map is useful even without a robot.
choices.outcome: You save the old flight route and leave the drone charging.

nodes.title: Voices in the vent
paragraphs: The ventilation shaft carries a second warning. This one is in your own voice: “The mirror is lying.”
Ren stares at the vent. “I do not remember you saying that.” Neither do you.

conditionalParagraphs.text: Ren taps your shoulder and says they'll trust your next move. That makes the vent's strange voice less frightening.

choices.label: Speak a question into the vent
choices.detail: See whether tomorrow can answer.
choices.outcome: The whisper replies: 'Follow the blue light, not the bright one.'

choices.label: Seal the vent and keep moving
choices.detail: Avoid adding your voice to the loop.
choices.outcome: The strange whisper fades. The station's speakers return to normal.

choices.label: Start the welcome ceremony
choices.detail: It's a little early, but it looks fun.

nodes.title: Tomorrow answers
paragraphs: Mika's voice returns, much clearer. “We're just outside the station,” they say. “I know that's impossible. I can see two Dock Sevens, and one is made of ice.”
Behind Mika, an alarm pulses in the Wren's cabin. You can hear someone counting backward.

choices.label: Ask for the real ship's coordinates
choices.detail: Find the Wren instead of its reflection.
choices.outcome: Mika reads the numbers twice. You finally have a place to send a signal.

choices.label: Talk Mika through the alarm
choices.detail: Help them think clearly.
choices.outcome: Mika's breathing slows. They promise to stay on the channel.

nodes.title: A copy of tomorrow
paragraphs: TAVI projects two possible arrival paths. One ends with the Wren docking safely. The other ends abruptly at the ice ring.
The computer calls the second path a 'predictive image.' No one asks whether the image came from a prediction or a memory.

conditionalParagraphs.text: You compare the two paths with the pulse that returned early. They fit together like pieces of a cracked window.

choices.label: Compare both paths
choices.detail: Search for the point where they split.
choices.outcome: The wrong turn happens seconds after the mirror flashes amber.

choices.label: Show the crew both paths
choices.detail: Get everyone on the same page.
choices.outcome: The crew stops arguing about whether the warning is real.

nodes.title: The second warning
paragraphs: A fresh transmission arrives from a second possible future. “Do not trust the rescue beacon,” says Mika, in a voice that sounds older by a hundred years.
Ren taps the screen. “How can there be two messages if we only have one tomorrow?”

choices.label: Check the new message's code
choices.detail: Make sure it really came from Mika.
choices.outcome: The code matches the Wren's emergency key. Both messages are real.

choices.label: Tell Mika about the contradiction
choices.detail: They deserve to know the whole danger.
choices.outcome: Mika says they'll watch for the false beacon and tell the captain.

choices.label: Put on the ancient test helmet
choices.detail: It might shield you from the storm.

nodes.title: The seedling crate
paragraphs: A cargo display shows a crate of rare Pel seedlings aboard the Wren. One holds the last living seeds of a tree lost from the planet's surface.
The crate's heat sensor is linked to the same guidance frequency as the docking mirror. That seems like an odd coincidence.

choices.label: Inspect the cargo signal
choices.detail: A crate shouldn't talk to a guidance beacon.
choices.outcome: The sensor is transmitting a tiny pulse—perfect for marking the real ship.

choices.label: Ask Mika to secure the seedlings
choices.detail: Protect the cargo while the ship maneuvers.
choices.outcome: Mika promises to strap down the crate before the final approach.

nodes.title: The ice ring
paragraphs: The Wren is close enough that you can see ice fragments spin around the station like pale feathers. Every fragment reflects the dock lights.
A single wrong flash could trick the ship into turning toward empty space.

choices.label: Measure the gaps between fragments
choices.detail: Find a corridor with fewer false reflections.
choices.outcome: You plot a narrow route through the brightest part of the storm.

choices.label: Turn off the outer work lights
choices.detail: Stop the reflections multiplying.
choices.outcome: The station darkens, but its emergency battery holds.

nodes.title: The broken translator
paragraphs: The docking console converts the ship's distress code into an instruction: OPEN HATCH. The original code actually means HOLD POSITION.
Someone reversed two symbols in the translator years ago. Every automatic docking system has copied the mistake.

choices.label: Fix the translation table
choices.detail: Prevent the same mistake on the next arrival.
choices.outcome: TAVI confirms the corrected code and starts checking the remaining messages.

choices.label: Ask the crew to use hand signals
choices.detail: Work around the broken software for now.
choices.outcome: Osei posts crew members at the window and sets up a manual signal board.

choices.label: Enable demonstration mode
choices.detail: Maybe the display will show more detail.

nodes.title: The captain's rule
paragraphs: Chief Osei gives you an orange clearance card. “A cadet can recommend a course,” they say. “But this time you're the one who has seen everything.”
They promise to back your decision if you can explain the risks.

conditionalParagraphs.text: Osei remembers the evidence you showed them at the start. They don't ask you to prove it twice.

choices.label: Explain every risk aloud
choices.detail: Everyone should understand what could go wrong.
choices.outcome: The bridge crew agrees to follow a single plan.

choices.label: Use the card to unlock the mirror
choices.detail: You'll need the control before the storm peaks.
choices.outcome: The mirror accepts your badge. A manual override appears.

nodes.title: Two maps, one destination
paragraphs: On the wall, Juno's paper map and TAVI's projected map refuse to line up. They agree on the planet, the station, and the ice—but not on the dock itself.
You realize one map is showing where the dock will be tomorrow.

choices.label: Combine the two maps
choices.detail: Make one route that accounts for both days.
choices.outcome: The safe path passes behind the station's shadow, not through the bright ice.

choices.label: Give Juno the pen
choices.detail: Let someone experienced draw the route.
choices.outcome: Juno finds an older approach line. The crew agrees to follow it.

nodes.title: A vote in Control
paragraphs: The crew gathers around the main console. Some want to shut the mirror off. Others want to send a rescue signal through it.
Ren reminds everyone that tomorrow's crew can hear what you do today.

choices.label: Ask everyone to agree on one signal
choices.detail: Keep the plan simple enough to work.
choices.outcome: The votes settle. For once, no one is talking over anyone else.

choices.label: Write a procedure on the screen
choices.detail: A shared checklist keeps surprises small.
choices.outcome: TAVI adds the safe-angle calculation and marks the dangerous switches.

choices.label: Step inside the chronology booth
choices.detail: It says TIME MACHINE in big letters.

nodes.title: The trade with time
paragraphs: TAVI has a proposal: send one strong signal now, and the Wren might never have to send its warning tomorrow. The price is half the station's spare power.
There is also a weaker signal. It won't change tomorrow, but it might guide the ship away from the ice.

choices.label: Prepare the strong signal
choices.detail: Spend power to change the future itself.
choices.outcome: The capacitor glows blue. TAVI calls it 'a very hopeful gamble.'

choices.label: Save the station's charge
choices.detail: A smaller plan can still be a good one.
choices.outcome: You keep the emergency circuit stable and mark the weaker signal frequency.

nodes.title: TAVI's impossible question
paragraphs: “If you warn tomorrow's crew and they never need to warn us,” TAVI asks, “who sent the first message?”
Nobody has an answer. The computer asks you to choose whether that matters more than the people aboard the Wren.

choices.label: Say the people matter most
choices.detail: The mystery can wait.
choices.outcome: TAVI seems relieved and assigns the rescue team to your plan.

choices.label: Find the first signal's source
choices.detail: Understanding the loop may help close it.
choices.outcome: The signal begins in the mirror's own memory bank.

nodes.title: The silent bell
paragraphs: The dock bell stops ringing, although the warning light is still red. TAVI says that in one possible tomorrow, the Wren has already turned away.
You have five minutes to decide whether to send a new signal. A slow silver pulse crosses the window.

choices.label: Test the bell's last recording
choices.detail: The silence might be another clue.
choices.outcome: You hear your own voice beneath Mika's: 'Use the blue light.'

choices.label: Bring the whole crew to the window
choices.detail: Make sure nobody is left guessing.
choices.outcome: Ren and Osei stand beside you. You won't make the last call alone.

choices.label: Ask the help desk to solve the storm
choices.detail: They promised twenty-four-hour support.

nodes.title: Seal or signal
paragraphs: A safety shutter closes over the end of Dock Seven. The station's protection system wants every door shut for the glass storm.
To send a rescue signal, someone will need to route it around that shutter.

choices.label: Route the signal through the old antenna
choices.detail: A longer path, but no need to open the dock.
choices.outcome: You find a clean channel to the Wren.

choices.label: Hold the shutter for a moment
choices.detail: Let the crew prepare the signal equipment.
choices.outcome: The crew makes room in the service corridor before the shutter comes down.

nodes.title: The last battery
paragraphs: Only two power cells remain in the console. One runs the outer mirror. The other keeps the emergency lights on in the station shelters.
Ren says you can take a cell from the antenna, but the climb will cost a minute.

choices.label: Leave shelter power untouched
choices.detail: People on the station come first.
choices.outcome: The emergency lights stay on. You find a smaller charge you can spare.

choices.label: Borrow the antenna cell
choices.detail: Take the risk yourself instead of darkening shelters.
choices.outcome: You get one extra pulse for the mirror's motor.

nodes.title: The reflection window
paragraphs: A shape slides across the glass: a ship with the Wren's silhouette, except its engines are dark. Its reflection moves in the wrong direction.
TAVI labels it ECHO, not SHIP. You press your palm against the cold window.

conditionalParagraphs.text: You recognize the dangerous silver curve from your earlier measurements. The false ship is following it exactly.

choices.label: Mark the echo's position
choices.detail: Keep the false ship out of your route.
choices.outcome: The echo's path gives you an exact angle to avoid.

choices.label: Warn Mika about the false shape
choices.detail: No one aboard should mistake it for home.
choices.outcome: Mika agrees to follow your voice rather than the bright outline.

choices.label: Try the emergency escape pod
choices.detail: You want another angle on the storm.

nodes.title: A pulse of silver
paragraphs: The storm is almost touching the mirror. A single burst of light can cut through it, but it may also make every piece of ice shine like a tiny false dock.
Your wrist radio vibrates. Mika is waiting.

choices.label: Synchronize the pulse with Mika
choices.detail: One shared count could keep both crews together.
choices.outcome: Mika whispers 'ready' and taps the same rhythm as your heart.

choices.label: Choose the measured frequency
choices.detail: The chart tells you where the light will go.
choices.outcome: Your waveform matches the map exactly. TAVI approves for the first time today.

nodes.title: The crew on the other side
paragraphs: You hear the Wren's captain give an order, and then Mika says, “We can see your station. For a second we can see it twice.”
Osei places a hand on the console. Nobody will take the decision away from you now.

choices.label: Send Mika your final route
choices.detail: Give the Wren a plan they can execute.
choices.outcome: Mika repeats the safe coordinates without a mistake.

choices.label: Ask the bridge crew to repeat your plan
choices.detail: Make sure everyone knows what will happen next.
choices.outcome: Three voices repeat the signal timing back to you.

nodes.title: No more warnings
paragraphs: The warning lights go steady. A calm voice says the Wren has reached the last approach point. The station can send one final command.
You remember the first message: DON'T OPEN THE DOOR. It never said not to turn on the light.

conditionalParagraphs.text: Mika says your name over the radio. You don't remember giving it to them, but the sound keeps you steady.

choices.label: Check every safety lock
choices.detail: Make sure no door opens by accident.
choices.outcome: All pressure doors remain sealed. The only thing you can change is the guide light.

choices.label: Tell Ren to guard the hatch
choices.detail: Someone should keep an eye on it.
choices.outcome: Ren gives you a two-finger salute and bolts the manual latch.

choices.label: Run the automatic victory test
choices.detail: Check whether the plan is good enough.

nodes.title: A very final broom closet
paragraphs: You pull the handle labeled EMERGENCY EXIT. The door swings inward. Beyond it is a broom closet, complete with a mop that falls dramatically onto your shoe.

nodes.title: The heroic snack break
paragraphs: You press CREW EMERGENCY and a tray of hot noodles arrives from the cafeteria. The crew is grateful. The Wren, sadly, is still in danger.

nodes.title: A map of the wrong station
paragraphs: You unfold the map marked SECRET ROUTE. It is a guide to the museum's model of Starport Nine. After three turns, you are standing in front of a very small plastic dock.

ending.title: THE END (OF THIS MAP)
ending.note: A real map would help more.

nodes.title: The automatic apology
paragraphs: The computer offers to apologize to tomorrow for the delay. You accept. It sends SORRY ABOUT THE WEATHER four thousand times and fills the message screen.

ending.title: THE END (OF THE INBOX)
ending.note: Cancel the apology and try again.

nodes.title: The twelve-second nap
paragraphs: A medical chair promises a quick rest. You sit. It locks into overnight recovery mode and begins playing whale songs. Ren pulls the plug before you fall asleep.

ending.title: THE END (OF YOUR NAP)
ending.note: You have a ship to save.

nodes.title: The victory parade
paragraphs: You press the green control marked CELEBRATE ARRIVAL. Confetti pours from the ceiling. The Wren has not arrived, but TAVI plays a trumpet fanfare anyway.

nodes.title: The spectacularly wrong helmet
paragraphs: The locker opens to reveal a helmet the size of a fishbowl. When you put it on, every voice sounds like a duck. Ren takes a picture for blackmail.

nodes.title: An upgrade nobody asked for
paragraphs: The mirror's software offers DELUXE DEMONSTRATION MODE. You agree. Every docking arrow becomes a dancing cartoon star. TAVI refuses to continue until you undo it.

nodes.title: The wrong kind of time machine
paragraphs: You step inside the archive's chronology booth. It stamps today's date on a paper wristband. That's all it does. The attendant asks whether you want a souvenir.

nodes.title: A rather permanent hold tune
paragraphs: You call the station's help line. It puts you on hold. At least the music is pleasant. TAVI estimates a six-month wait for an operator.

ending.title: THE END (OF THE CALL)
ending.note: Hang up before the next song.

nodes.title: The brave escape pod
paragraphs: You enter the escape pod to inspect the windows. A voice announces, 'This pod is decorative.' The door opens onto a gift shop.

nodes.title: The fake finish line
paragraphs: The console flashes YOU HAVE WON and plays a little tune. The letters below say TRAINING SIMULATION COMPLETE. The actual Wren is still waiting outside.

ending.title: THE END (OF THE TRAINING)
ending.note: The real final call is still ahead.

nodes.title: Your call, cadet
paragraphs: Thirty-six decisions have brought you to the same impossible minute. Dock Seven is sealed. The Wren's lights show through the storm, sometimes doubled, sometimes gone.
You have clues, people who trust you, and whatever station power you've managed to save. The choice you make now cannot be undone. TAVI doesn't offer a suggestion. Neither does Chief Osei.
From the radio, Mika asks one simple question: “Which light is real?”

conditionalParagraphs.text: You remember Mika's counted pulse. It could connect the real ship to the real dock.

choices.label: Send the true route together
choices.detail: Guide the Wren with the corrected light and both crews in sync.
choices.outcome: The blue light reaches both days at once.

choices.label: Guide the Wren around the ice
choices.detail: Take the long approach, even if the time loop stays unsolved.
choices.outcome: The ship follows the older map, slowly and carefully.

choices.label: Force the old mirror into position
choices.detail: Use the reserve charge for one risky flash.
choices.outcome: The mirror moves with a grinding cry.

choices.label: Close the guide lights and delay arrival
choices.detail: Keep the station safe, but turn away the Wren.
choices.outcome: The bridge shutters darken the stars.

choices.label: Open the main hatch and follow the brightest light
choices.detail: Ignore the warning and trust the easiest-looking path.
choices.outcome: The bright line across the ice is not a docking lane.

nodes.title: Tomorrow arrives safely
paragraphs: You count with Mika: three fast beats, one slow. The outer mirror answers in the exact rhythm you measured, and the ice ring goes dark for one perfect second.
Through the silver storm, the Wren's real lights appear. Not a reflection. Not a memory. Chief Osei guides the ship into Dock Seven without opening the hatch until the pressure display reads SAFE.

The next morning the Wren arrives on schedule anyway. Mika steps off carrying the first Pel seedling and says, “I think we fixed tomorrow yesterday.” TAVI suggests that this sentence is illegal in several branches of mathematics.
The station's old mirror is rebuilt. The seedlings will grow. Ren keeps the note you wrote during the storm and tapes it above the new console: BELIEVE THE SIGNAL. CHECK THE LIGHT.

ending.title: Tomorrow arrives safely
ending.note: BEST OUTCOME · Everyone arrives, and the time loop is closed.

nodes.title: The long way home
paragraphs: You choose the older approach route, away from the sharpest ice. Mika repeats the bearings, and the Wren turns into the dark shadow behind the station.
It takes almost a full day to reach the dock. No one complains. When the Wren finally lands, its passengers are tired and hungry, but unharmed. The seedlings survive the delay.
The first warning remains on your wrist radio, though nobody remembers sending it. Chief Osei calls this a mystery worth keeping. TAVI calls it a flaw in the universe's filing system.
Mika asks to see the glass storm from the observation deck. You stand beside them and watch a silver ribbon fade into space.

ending.title: The long way home
ending.note: GREAT OUTCOME · Everyone is safe, but the mystery remains.

nodes.title: A hard landing
paragraphs: You swing the old mirror into position using the reserve cells. For one breathless moment the signal vanishes. Then the Wren shoots out of the silver fog at a dangerous angle.
The docking clamps catch the ship just in time. The Wren's crew gets out safely, with the seedling crates mostly intact. But the outer mirror snaps in half and the station loses power to three decks.
Ren spends the next week helping repair Starport Nine. Chief Osei thanks you for making the dangerous choice that brought the Wren home, then points out the long list of repairs it caused.
Mika finds you under the broken mirror and says, “Next time, maybe we use the long way around.” You agree. Next time you'll know more.

ending.title: A hard landing
ending.note: MIXED OUTCOME · The crew survives, but Starport Nine pays the price.

nodes.title: The empty docking bay
paragraphs: You darken the guidance lights and seal the dock. The false reflections disappear. So does the Wren's reply.

For two terrible hours there is no voice on the radio. Then another station catches Mika's message: the Wren has turned back toward Pel. Its crew is safe, but the seedlings must return to storage and the research mission is cancelled.
Chief Osei says that protecting the people already on Starport Nine was a defensible choice. It doesn't feel like a victory. The empty dock bell rings once more, then never again.
You keep the old map and Mika's message. One day there may be a chance to try again—with better evidence and a little more courage.

ending.title: The empty docking bay
ending.note: POOR OUTCOME · The station is safe, but the ship must turn away.

nodes.title: The light that lied
paragraphs: You open the hatch and follow the brightest light. For one second it looks like a clear route. Then the reflection folds, and the real ship disappears behind the ice ring.
The station's safety field slams shut. A shock travels through the outer deck. The crew evacuates and Starport Nine survives, damaged but intact. The Wren does not answer any of the rescue calls.

Search ships are launched immediately. Days later, they are still looking. Nobody says the word lost aloud, but the empty dock is quieter than it was before. The glass storm has taken the ship somewhere nobody can find.
TAVI saves the first warning in the permanent log. You listen to it once more: “Don't open the door.” Next time, you promise yourself, you will hear the whole message before you act.

ending.title: The light that lied
ending.note: WORST OUTCOME · A reckless choice loses the Wren and endangers the station.
